question.text: Zephyr Long-Short Fund (Cat III) is planning to trade listed equity derivatives with 2x leverage. The CIO is negotiating terms with a Prime Broker. Which bundle of services is MOST characteristic of the Prime Broker's role for a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Margin financing, securities lending/borrowing, centralised clearing, consolidated trade reporting and leverage facilities.
Appointment of the statutory auditor and signing the annual report.
Filing the PPM with SEBI and obtaining the due diligence certificate.
Drafting the LPA and contribution agreements for investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III hedge funds use a Prime Broker for margin financing, securities lending, clearing/settlement, consolidated trade and P&L reporting, and leverage support. While the chapter does not carve out a separate PB section, Cat III AIFs explicitly rely on PB services distinct from the custodian's safekeeping role (custody of goods in physical settlement of commodity derivatives is the custodian's piece). The Trap: Option B is auditor role. Option C is merchant banker. Option D is legal counsel. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) tests margining mechanics; XIX-B tests Cat III distribution; XIX-C ties it together from the Manager's PB negotiation lens. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate your PB fee as basis points on average gross assets, NOT on notional leverage. A PB paid on notional has an incentive to push you into higher leverage — structural conflict.
